report.source_text: Our patient was treated conservatively with ceftriaxone for antimicrobial coverage and amlodipine for blood pressure management. Six days after admission and treatment, the boy was asymptomatic, however, with minimal hematuria.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old male presented with fever, headache, vomiting, blurry vision, and seizures. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, decreased complement 3, elevated ASO titers, uremia, hematuria, and proteinuria indicating post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. Blood pressure was elevated at 150/100 mmHg on admission and remained high during 72-hour monitoring. Brain MRI demonstrated symmetrical enhancement in occipital and temporal watershed regions consistent with posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Neurological exam showed decreased left eye visual acuity but was otherwise unremarkable. The patient was treated with ceftriaxone and amlodipine, leading to symptom resolution by six days, with minimal residual hematuria.
